speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin my assessment, have you experienced any fractures from minor injuries or significant heights, and did they heal unusually slowly?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Classic Salt-Wasting or Simple Virilizing type) causing ambiguous genitalia and primary amenorrhea due to enzyme deficiency (likely 21-hydroxylase), leading to androgen excess and bone fragility.
